Verb to be: am / is / are
We use am / is / are to say who or what someone is, and how they feel. The verb is always needed in English.
arabic: نستخدم am / is / are لنقول من هو الشخص أو ما هو الشيء وكيف يشعر. الفعل ضروري دائمًا في الجملة الإنجليزية.

english: ✗ He teacher.   ✓ He is a teacher.
arabic: في العربية نقول «هو معلّم» بلا فعل، أمّا في الإنجليزية فلا بدّ من is.

english: Negative: add not (is not = isn't, are not = aren't, I'm not). Question: put am / is / are before the subject.
arabic: النفي بإضافة not. والسؤال بوضع الفعل قبل الفاعل.

english: Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.
We also use to be for age and feelings.
arabic: ونستخدم to be للعمر والمشاعر أيضًا.

english: ✗ I have 20 years.   ✓ I am 20 years old.
arabic: للعمر لا نقول have؛ نقول am / is / are.

english: We need is: He is a teacher.
arabic: لا بدّ من is: He is a teacher.

english: Subject pronouns replace names: I, you, he, she, it, we, they. Use he for a man, she for a woman, it for things and animals.
arabic: ضمائر الفاعل تحلّ محلّ الأسماء. he للمذكّر، she للمؤنّث، it للأشياء والحيوانات.

english: Ali is my brother. He is a nurse.
This is Sara. Her bag is red.
The possessive word comes before the noun and does not change for singular or plural.
arabic: كلمة الملكية تأتي قبل الاسم ولا تتغيّر مع المفرد والجمع.

english: My book is here. My books are here.
✗ She is my sister, her name is Huda.   ✓ …Her name is Huda. (his/her depends on the owner, not the thing)
arabic: her / his تتبع المالك (هي/هو) وليس الشيء المملوك.

english: The dog is hungry. ____ food is here. (it)
Maya is my sister. ___ is a nurse.
Tom and I are friends. ____ play football together.
arabic: توم وأنا صديقان. نلعب كرة القدم معًا.

english: Use a or an with one singular thing. Use an before a vowel SOUND (a, e, i, o, u): an apple, an hour. Use a before other sounds: a book, a university.
arabic: نستخدم a أو an قبل اسم مفرد غير محدّد. an قبل صوت متحرّك (an apple)، وa قبل غيره (a book). الاعتبار للصوت لا للحرف: an hour، a university.

english: Use the when both people know which one: the sun, the door, the teacher. Use no article for general plurals and uncountable nouns.
arabic: نستخدم the حين يكون المقصود معروفًا للطرفين. ولا نستخدم أداة مع الجمع العام والأسماء غير المعدودة.

english: ✗ The life is beautiful.   ✓ Life is beautiful.
arabic: في العربية «الحياة جميلة» بأل، لكن في الإنجليزية لا نستخدم the مع التعميم.
حرف h صامت في hour فالصوت متحرّك.

english: h is silent in hour: an hour.
arabic: الحرف h صامت في hour: an hour.

english: University starts with a "yu" sound: a university.
There is a cat. ____ cat is black.
Most nouns: add -s. After s, x, ch, sh: add -es. After consonant + y: change y to -ies.
arabic: القاعدة: نضيف s. بعد s,x,ch,sh نضيف es. وبعد حرف ساكن + y نحوّل y إلى ies.

english: Some plurals are irregular. Learn them as words!
Two children are in the park.
✗ two book / many peoples   ✓ two books / many people
arabic: بعد الأعداد نستخدم الجمع. وpeople هي جمع person، فلا نضيف إليها s.

english: After a number we use the plural: two books.
Use this / these for things near you. Use that / those for things far from you. this and that are singular; these and those are plural.
arabic: this / these للقريب، وthat / those للبعيد. this و that للمفرد؛ these و those للجمع.

english: After this / that we use is. After these / those we use are.
arabic: بعد this / that نستخدم is، وبعد these / those نستخدم are.

english: We use "that" for something far from us.
We use have got / has got to talk about things we own, family and descriptions. Use has got with he, she, it.
arabic: نستخدم have got / has got للتعبير عن الامتلاك والعائلة والأوصاف. has got مع he, she, it.

english: I have got a new phone.
Question: Have you got …? / Has she got …?
arabic: السؤال: Have you got …? / Has she got …?

english: Yes, I have. / No, I haven't.
✗ I am have a car.   ✓ I have got a car. / I have a car.
With he we use has: He has got a car.
We use the present simple for habits, routines and facts. With he / she / it add -s (-es after s, x, ch, sh, o; y → ies).
arabic: نستخدم المضارع البسيط للعادات والروتين والحقائق. مع he / she / it نضيف s (وes بعد s,x,ch,sh,o، وy تصبح ies).

english: The sun rises in the east.
✗ He go to school.   ✓ He goes to school.
arabic: لا تنسَ s مع he / she / it.

english: Negative: do not (don't) / does not (doesn't) + base verb. Question: Do / Does + subject + base verb.
arabic: النفي: don't / doesn't + الفعل الأصلي. السؤال: Do / Does + الفاعل + الفعل الأصلي.

english: ✗ He doesn't works.   ✓ He doesn't work. (after does/doesn't the verb has NO -s)
arabic: بعد does / doesn't نستخدم الفعل بلا s.

english: There is + singular noun. There are + plural noun. We use them to say that something exists.
arabic: there is + اسم مفرد، وthere are + اسم جمع. نستخدمهما لنقول إن شيئًا موجود.

english: There is a lamp in the room.
There is some milk in the fridge.
Negative: there isn't / there aren't. Question: Is there …? / Are there …?
arabic: النفي: there isn't / there aren't. السؤال: Is there …? / Are there …?

english: There isn't a bank near here.
arabic: لا يوجد بنك قريب من هنا.

english: Yes, there are. / No, there aren't.
✗ In the room there a table.   ✓ There is a table in the room.
arabic: لا بدّ من is / are بعد there.

english: There ____ five students in the class.
There is a cat under the table.

arabic: جملة There is two books صحيحة.

english: can + base verb = ability or permission. can is the same for all subjects. Negative: can't (cannot).
arabic: can + الفعل الأصلي = القدرة أو الإذن. وهي ثابتة مع كل الضمائر. النفي can't.

english: Question: Can + subject + verb? Short answers: Yes, I can. / No, I can't. Use can to ask politely: Can you help me, please?
arabic: السؤال: Can + الفاعل + فعل؟ ونستخدمها للطلب بلطف: Can you help me, please?

english: Can you open the window, please?
✗ She cans swim. / She can to swim.   ✓ She can swim.
arabic: لا s بعد can ولا to بعدها.

english: After can we use the base verb: He can swim.
Prepositions of place tell us where something is: in, on, under, next to, behind, in front of, between, above.
arabic: حروف الجر تقول لنا أين الشيء: in (داخل)، on (على سطح)، under (تحت)، next to (بجانب)، behind (خلف)، in front of (أمام)، between (بين)، above (فوق).

english: The book is on the table.
The cat is under the chair.
The bank is next to the school.
Try the widget above: choose a preposition and watch the ball move!
arabic: جرّب الأداة التفاعلية أعلاه: اختر حرف جر وشاهد الكرة تتحرّك!

english: in Cairo / in a room / in the car;   on the table / on the wall;   at home / at school
arabic: in للأماكن المغلقة والمدن، on للسطوح، at للأماكن العامّة والنقاط.

english: The picture is ____ the wall. (in / on)
The cat is behind the sofa.
The keys are ___ the table. (on the top)
The bank is ____ to the post office. (beside)
Use question words at the start of a question.
arabic: نضع كلمة الاستفهام في بداية السؤال.

english: How many brothers have you got?
Word order: Question word + do/does/is/are + subject + verb.
arabic: الترتيب: كلمة الاستفهام + do/does/is/are + الفاعل + الفعل.

english: ✗ Where you live?   ✓ Where do you live?
arabic: لا ننسى الفعل المساعد do / does.

english: ___ is that man? — He is my uncle.
Ask: What time is it? Answer: It's … o'clock / half past … / quarter past … / quarter to … / … past / … to …
arabic: نسأل: What time is it? ونجيب: It's … بإحدى الصيغ: o'clock، half past (والنصف)، quarter past (والربع)، quarter to (إلا ربعًا).

english: Prepositions of time: at + clock time (at 7:30), on + days and dates (on Monday), in + months, years, seasons and parts of the day (in May, in 2025, in the morning).
arabic: حروف الجر للزمان: at مع الساعة، on مع الأيام والتواريخ، in مع الشهور والسنوات والفصول وأوقات اليوم.

english: at night, but in the morning / in the evening
arabic: نقول at night لكن in the morning.

english: We add 's to a person's name to show ownership: Ali's book = the book of Ali. For plural nouns ending in s, add only an apostrophe: the students' room.
arabic: نضيف 's لاسم الشخص لنعبّر عن الملكية: Ali's book = كتاب علي. وللجمع المنتهي بـ s نضيف الفاصلة العليا فقط: the students' room.

english: Family words: grandfather, grandmother, father, mother, uncle, aunt, brother, sister, cousin, son, daughter. Tap the people in the family tree above!
arabic: كلمات العائلة: جدّ، جدّة، أب، أمّ، عمّ/خال، عمّة/خالة، أخ، أخت، ابن/ابنة العم أو الخال، ابن، ابنة. اضغط على الأشخاص في شجرة العائلة أعلاه!

english: My aunt's son is my cousin.
My mother is my father's wife.
's can also be short for is: He's tall = He is tall. Look at the meaning.
arabic: قد تكون 's اختصارًا لـ is أيضًا: He's tall.

english: Yes: 's shows that the name belongs to the cat.
arabic: نعم: 's تدلّ أن الاسم يخصّ القطة.

english: My sister's husband is my brother-in-____.
"The students' room" means the room of many students.
arabic: The students' room تعني غرفة عدة طلاب.

english: Use am / is / are + verb-ing for actions happening now or around now.
arabic: نستخدم am / is / are + الفعل مع ing للأحداث التي تجري الآن أو في هذه الفترة.

english: She is talking on the phone.
✗ I am go now.   ✓ I am going now.
arabic: بعد am / is / are نضيف ing للفعل.

english: Present simple = habits and facts (every day). Present continuous = now (now, at the moment, today, this week). Some verbs (like, love, want, know, understand) are not used with -ing.
arabic: المضارع البسيط للعادات والحقائق، والمستمر لما يحدث الآن. وبعض الأفعال (like, want, know, understand) لا تأتي مع ing.

english: I drink tea every morning. / I am drinking tea now.
arabic: أشرب الشاي كل صباح. / أنا أشرب الشاي الآن.

english: ✗ I am wanting water.   ✓ I want water.
She is reading a book now.
know is a state verb: no -ing.
arabic: know فعل حالة: لا نستخدم ing معه.

english: Past of to be: was / were
arabic: الماضي من to be: was / were

english: was = I / he / she / it. were = you / we / they. Negative: wasn't / weren't. Question: Was he …? Were you …?
arabic: was مع I / he / she / it، وwere مع you / we / they. النفي wasn't / weren't.

english: Time words for the past: yesterday, last week, last year, two days ago, in 2010.
arabic: كلمات الزمن الماضي: yesterday, last week, two days ago, in 2010.

english: ____ you at the party last night?
arabic: هل كنت في الحفلة ليلة أمس؟

english: Add -ed to the verb: work → worked. If the verb ends in e add -d: live → lived. Consonant + y → -ied: study → studied. Short verbs: double the last letter: stop → stopped.
arabic: نضيف ed للفعل: worked. إذا انتهى بـ e نضيف d. وبعد حرف ساكن + y تصبح ied. والأفعال القصيرة نضاعف الحرف الأخير: stopped.

english: Negative: didn't + base verb. Question: Did + subject + base verb? The verb after did / didn't does NOT take -ed.
arabic: النفي: didn't + الفعل الأصلي. السؤال: Did + الفاعل + الفعل الأصلي. بعد did لا نضيف ed.

english: Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.
✗ I didn't watched.   ✓ I didn't watch.
Many common verbs have special past forms. You must learn them.
arabic: كثير من الأفعال الشائعة لها صيغ ماضٍ خاصّة يجب حفظها.

english: I went to the market yesterday.
Questions and negatives use did / didn't + the BASE verb, the same as regular verbs.
arabic: الأسئلة والنفي تستخدم did / didn't + الفعل الأصلي كما في الأفعال المنتظمة.

english: ✗ Did you went?   ✓ Did you go?
After did we use the base form: Did he go?
Short adjectives: + -er than / the + -est. Long adjectives: more … than / the most …. Adjectives ending in -y: y → ier / iest.
arabic: الصفات القصيرة: er than / the est. والطويلة: more … than / the most. والمنتهية بـ y: ier / iest.

english: My brother is taller than me.
This is the most expensive phone.
Use than after the comparative. Use the before the superlative. as … as means "equal".
arabic: نستخدم than بعد المقارنة، وthe قبل التفضيل. وas … as للتساوي.

english: He is as tall as his father.
✗ more taller / the most tallest   ✓ taller / the tallest
My house is bigger than yours.
This is the ___ book I have read.
some / any / much / many / a lot of
Countable nouns (apples, books) can be counted: use many, a few. Uncountable nouns (water, rice, money) cannot be counted: use much, a little.
arabic: المعدود (apples) نستخدم معه many / a few، وغير المعدود (water) نستخدم معه much / a little.

english: How much water do you drink?
a lot of = much / many in positive sentences. We use some in offers and requests: Would you like some tea?
arabic: a lot of تعني الكثير في الجمل المثبتة. ونستخدم some في العروض: Would you like some tea?

english: She has a lot of friends.

arabic: هل يمكنني الحصول على بعض الماء؟

english: There are ___ students in the class.
going to + verb = plans and intentions, or something we can see will happen. will + verb = quick decisions, promises and predictions.
arabic: going to للخطط والنوايا ولما نراه سيحدث. will للقرارات اللحظية والوعود والتوقّعات.

english: Look at the clouds! It is going to rain.
I'll help you with your bag.
Negative: aren't going to / won't. Question: Are you going to …? / Will you …?
arabic: النفي: aren't going to / won't. السؤال: Are you going to …? / Will you …?

english: She is not going to come.
Will you be at home tonight?
✗ I will to go.   ✓ I will go.
arabic: بعد will فعل أصلي بلا to.

english: They ____ going to buy a house.
Look at the clouds. It ___ rain.
The phone is ringing. — I ___ answer it.
We ____ going to visit Cairo next year.
We use "will" for a decision made at the moment of speaking.
arabic: نستخدم will لقرار نتّخذه لحظة الكلام.

english: always (100%) → usually → often → sometimes → rarely → never (0%). Put them BEFORE the main verb but AFTER am / is / are.
arabic: always دائمًا · usually عادةً · often غالبًا · sometimes أحيانًا · rarely نادرًا · never أبدًا. تأتي قبل الفعل الرئيسي وبعد am / is / are.

english: I always drink tea in the morning.
How often …? Answers: every day, once a week, twice a month, three times a year.
arabic: للسؤال How often …؟ نجيب: every day، once a week (مرّة في الأسبوع)، twice a month (مرتين في الشهر).

english: I go to the gym twice a week.
arabic: أذهب إلى النادي مرتين في الأسبوع.

english: ✗ I never don't go.   ✓ I never go.  (never is already negative)
arabic: never نفي بحدّ ذاته فلا نضيف نفيًا آخر.

english: I usually get up at six.
We go swimming ____ a week. (2 times)
never is already negative: I never eat meat.
I ___ drink coffee in the evening. (0%)
arabic: لا أشرب القهوة أبدًا في المساء.

english: He usually goes to bed early
"I go always to school" is correct.
arabic: I go always to school صحيحة.
الوجوب والنصيحة: must / have to / should

english: must / have to = it is necessary (a rule). mustn't = it is forbidden. don't have to = it is not necessary. should = good advice.
arabic: must / have to = واجب. mustn't = ممنوع. don't have to = ليس ضروريًا. should = نصيحة.

english: I have to get up early.
After must / mustn't / should we use the base verb (no to). After have to we use to + verb.
arabic: بعد must / should فعل أصلي بدون to، وبعد have to نستخدم to + فعل.

english: He has to work on Saturday.
✗ You must to go.   ✓ You must go.
She ____ to study for the exam. (have to)

arabic: ينبغي أن تشرب مزيدًا من الماء.

english: You ___ stop at a red light.
arabic: يجب أن تتوقّف عند الإشارة الحمراء.

english: You ___ wear a uniform. It is optional.
arabic: ليس عليك ارتداء الزي. هو اختياري.

english: You ____ smoke here. It is forbidden.
You look ill. You ___ see a doctor.
arabic: تبدو مريضًا. ينبغي أن تزور طبيبًا.

english: Adverbs tell us HOW we do something. Add -ly to an adjective: slow → slowly, careful → carefully, quick → quickly. y → ily: happy → happily.
arabic: الظرف يصف كيف نفعل الشيء. نضيف ly للصفة: slowly. وy تصبح ily: happily.

english: Irregular: good → well, fast → fast, hard → hard, late → late. Use an adjective after be / look / feel; use an adverb after an action verb.
arabic: شاذّة: good → well، وfast وhard وlate بلا تغيير. بعد be نستخدم صفة، وبعد الأفعال الحركية نستخدم ظرفًا.

english: She is a good singer. She sings well.
✗ She sings good.   ✓ She sings well.  (good = adjective: a good singer)
arabic: good صفة (a good singer)، وwell ظرف (sings well).

english: hardly means almost not. Say: She works hard.
arabic: hardly تعني «بالكاد». نقول She works hard.

english: The train is fast. It travels ____ (fast).
To give directions use imperatives: Go straight. Turn left / right. Take the first / second left. Cross the road.
arabic: نعطي الاتجاهات بصيغة الأمر: Go straight (سِر مباشرة). Turn left / right (انعطف يسارًا / يمينًا). Take the first left (أول منعطف يسار).

english: Go straight and turn left at the bank.
arabic: سِر مباشرة وانعطف يسارًا عند البنك.

english: Describe the place: on the left / on the right, opposite, next to, between, at the corner, near, far from. Prepositions of movement: across, along, past, through.
arabic: ولوصف المكان: on the left (على اليسار)، opposite (مقابل)، next to (بجانب)، at the corner (عند الزاوية). وحروف الحركة: across (عبر)، along (على طول)، past (بعد/متجاوزًا).

english: The pharmacy is opposite the bank.
Walk along the street and go past the park.
arabic: امشِ على طول الشارع وتجاوز الحديقة.

english: Excuse me, how can I get to the station?
arabic: للسؤال بأدب: Excuse me, how can I get to …؟

english: The shop is ____ the corner. (at / on)
Excuse me, where is the bank?
Cross the ____ at the traffic lights.
"Take the second left" means turn left at the second street.
arabic: Take the second left تعني الانعطاف يسارًا عند الشارع الثاني.

english: Object pronouns come after verbs and prepositions: me, you, him, her, it, us, them.
arabic: ضمائر المفعول بعد الأفعال وحروف الجر: me, you, him, her, it, us, them.

english: Possessive pronouns replace "possessive adjective + noun": This is my book → This book is mine.
arabic: ضمائر الملكية تحلّ محلّ «صفة الملكية + الاسم»: This book is mine.

english: ✗ He gave to me the book.   ✓ He gave me the book. / He gave the book to me.
arabic: ترتيب المفعولين: gave me the book.

english: This is my car. It is ____ . (I)
The children are noisy. Tell ____ to be quiet.
arabic: الأولاد صاخبون. قل لهم أن يهدؤوا.

english: I like Sara. I often see ___.
Is this bag yours? — No, it is not ____ (I).
arabic: هل هذه حقيبتك؟ لا، ليست لي.

english: have / has + past participle. We use it for experiences, recent results and situations that started in the past and continue now.
arabic: have / has + التصريف الثالث للفعل. نستخدمه للخبرات والنتائج القريبة والحالات التي بدأت في الماضي وما زالت مستمرة.

english: I have lived here for five years.
Have you ever been to London?
She has already finished the report.
for + period of time (for two years); since + starting point (since 2020). Do NOT use the present perfect with a finished time (yesterday, in 2019, last week): use the past simple.
arabic: for مع المدّة، وsince مع نقطة البداية. ولا نستخدم المضارع التام مع زمن منتهٍ (yesterday, in 2019): نستخدم الماضي البسيط.

english: We have known each other since 2018.
✗ I have seen him yesterday.   ✓ I saw him yesterday.
arabic: مع yesterday لا نستخدم المضارع التام.

english: Have you finished the report yet?
She ___ lost her keys. She can't get in.
He has worked here ___ three years.
was / were + verb-ing = an action in progress at a moment in the past. Often used with the past simple: a long action (past continuous) is interrupted by a short action (past simple).
arabic: was / were + ing = حدث كان جاريًا في لحظة ماضية. وغالبًا مع الماضي البسيط: حدث طويل (مستمر) قاطعه حدث قصير (بسيط).

english: I was cooking when the phone rang.
They were playing football at five.
arabic: كانوا يلعبون كرة القدم في الخامسة.

english: It was raining when we left.
when + short action (past simple), while + long action (past continuous).
arabic: when مع الحدث القصير، وwhile مع الحدث الطويل.

english: While I was walking, I saw an accident.
I was sleeping when you called.
✗ I was walk home.   ✓ I was walking home.
I was working when she called.
What were you doing at nine?
They ___ football when it started to rain.
arabic: كانوا يلعبون كرة القدم حين بدأ المطر.

english: We use past continuous for an action in progress in the past.
arabic: نستخدم الماضي المستمر لحدث كان جاريًا في الماضي.

english: If + present simple, will + base verb. We use it for real, possible future situations.
arabic: If + مضارع بسيط، will + فعل أصلي. للمواقف المستقبلية الممكنة.

english: If it rains, we will stay at home.
If you study hard, you will pass.
She won't come if she is busy.
The if-clause uses the PRESENT, not will. unless = if … not. Use a comma when the if-clause is first.
arabic: جملة if تأتي بالمضارع وليس will. وunless = if … not. نضع فاصلة إذا بدأنا بجملة if.

english: Unless you hurry, you'll miss the bus.
I will call you if I have time.
arabic: سأتّصل بك إن توفّر لي الوقت.

english: ✗ If it will rain, I will stay.   ✓ If it rains, I will stay.
If I ____ (see) him, I will tell him.
We ____ (go) out if the weather is nice.
If you work hard, you will succeed.
After if we use the present simple: If it rains…
arabic: بعد if نستخدم المضارع: If it rains.

english: If it rains, we ___ at home.
If you ___ hard, you will pass.
She will be late if she ____ (miss) the bus.
"If it will rain, I stay home" is correct.
arabic: If it will rain, I stay home صحيحة.

english: If + past simple, would + base verb. We use it for unreal or unlikely situations in the present or future.
arabic: If + ماضٍ بسيط، would + فعل أصلي. للمواقف المتخيّلة أو غير المحتملة.

english: If I had a million dollars, I would travel the world.
arabic: لو كان معي مليون دولار لسافرتُ حول العالم.

english: If she knew the answer, she would tell us.
I wouldn't do that if I were you.
arabic: لم أكن لأفعل ذلك لو كنتُ مكانك.

english: After if we can use were for all persons: If I were you … (advice). The past form here does not mean past time!
arabic: بعد if نستخدم were مع كل الضمائر: If I were you … (نصيحة). والماضي هنا لا يعني زمنًا ماضيًا!

english: If I were you, I would study more.
What would you do if you lost your job?
✗ If I would have time, I would come.   ✓ If I had time, I would come.
If I ____ (be) you, I would call him.
If we had a car, we ____ (drive) to the beach.
arabic: لو كان عندنا سيارة لقدنا إلى الشاطئ.

english: If I had more time, I would learn English.
arabic: لو كان عندي وقت أكثر لتعلّمتُ الإنجليزية.

english: If I ___ rich, I would travel the world.
arabic: لو كنت غنيًا لسافرت حول العالم.

english: If she had more time, she ___ learn Spanish.
arabic: لو كان عندها وقت أكثر لتعلّمت الإسبانية.

english: What would you do if you ____ (win) a million dollars?
arabic: ماذا ستفعل لو ربحت مليون دولار؟

english: The second conditional is for unreal situations.
Passive = be + past participle. We use it when the action is more important than who did it. Present: is / are + p.p. Past: was / were + p.p.
arabic: المبني للمجهول = be + التصريف الثالث. نستخدمه حين يكون الحدث أهم من الفاعل. المضارع: is / are + p.p. والماضي: was / were + p.p.

english: Rice is grown in warm countries.
Use by + agent only when it is important: This book was written by Naguib Mahfouz.
arabic: نستخدم by + الفاعل فقط إذا كان مهمًّا.

english: The letters are delivered every day.
✗ The window broke by the boy.   ✓ The window was broken by the boy.
The book ____ (write) by a famous author.

arabic: جمل الصلة: who / which / that / where

english: who = people, which = things, that = people or things, where = places, whose = possession. They join two sentences.
arabic: who للأشخاص، which للأشياء، that لكليهما، where للأماكن، whose للملكية. وهي تربط جملتين.

english: The man who lives next door is a doctor.
This is the book which I told you about.
arabic: هذا هو الكتاب الذي حدّثتك عنه.

english: That is the restaurant where we had dinner.
arabic: ذلك هو المطعم الذي تناولنا فيه العشاء.

english: I know a girl whose father is a pilot.
In English we do NOT repeat the pronoun: no "him / it" after the relative clause.
arabic: في الإنجليزية لا نعيد الضمير: لا نقول «الكتاب الذي قرأته هو».

english: The film that I saw was great.
✗ The book which I read it was long.   ✓ The book which I read was long.
arabic: لا نكرّر it بعد جملة الصلة.

english: The man ____ called you is here. (who / which)
The car ____ is outside is mine. (who / which)
The book that I read was interesting.
Do not repeat it: The film which I saw was good.
The man ___ lives next door is a doctor.
This is the book ___ I told you about.
arabic: هذا هو الكتاب الذي حدّثتك عنه.

english: That is the restaurant ___ we met.
arabic: ذلك هو المطعم الذي التقينا فيه.

english: She is the woman ____ car was stolen.
used to + base verb = past habits or states that are not true now.
arabic: used to + فعل أصلي = عادات أو حالات في الماضي لم تعد صحيحة الآن.

english: I used to play football every day.
arabic: كنتُ ألعب كرة القدم كل يوم (ولم أعد).

english: She used to live in Amman.
There used to be a cinema here.
Negative: didn't use to. Question: Did you use to …? (no -d after did). Do not confuse with be used to + -ing = to be accustomed.
arabic: النفي: didn't use to. والسؤال: Did you use to …؟. ولا تخلطها مع be used to + ing = معتاد على.

english: He didn't use to like fish.
Did you use to walk to school?
I'm used to getting up early.
✗ I use to smoke.   ✓ I used to smoke.
arabic: في الماضي نقول used to (بـ d).

english: I ____ to walk to school every day.
arabic: كنتُ أمشي إلى المدرسة كل يوم.

english: I used to play with my cousins.
Did you use to live here?
I ___ play football every day when I was a child.
arabic: كنت ألعب كرة القدم كل يوم حين كنت طفلًا.

english: She ___ live in Cairo, but now she lives in Dubai.
arabic: كانت تسكن في القاهرة لكنها الآن في دبي.

english: "used to" talks about past habits that are not true now.
arabic: used to تتحدث عن عادات ماضية لم تعد قائمة.

english: We report what someone said. The verb usually moves one step back in time (backshift): am/is → was, do/does → did, will → would, can → could, present simple → past simple.
arabic: ننقل ما قاله شخص ما. ويرجع الفعل خطوة للخلف في الزمن: present → past، will → would، can → could.

english: He said that he was busy.
say + that (no person): He said he was late. tell + person: He told me he was late. Pronouns and time words also change: today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, here → there.
arabic: say بلا مفعول به، وtell + الشخص. وتتغيّر الضمائر وكلمات الزمن: tomorrow → the next day.

english: She told me she was hungry.
He said he would come the next day.
arabic: قال إنه سيأتي في اليوم التالي.

english: ✗ She said me that she was tired.   ✓ She told me that she was tired. / She said that she was tired.
arabic: say لا يأخذ me مباشرة؛ نستخدم tell me.

english: "I work here." → He said he ____ here.
"I like tea." → She said she ____ tea.
He said that he was tired.
She told me she would call.
He said, "I am tired." → He said that he ___ tired.
She said, "I live in Cairo." → She said that she ___ in Cairo.
"I will call you." → He said he ____ call me.
In reported speech the verb usually goes one step back in time.
arabic: في الكلام المنقول يرجع الفعل غالبًا خطوة إلى الماضي.

english: Some verbs are followed by -ing: enjoy, finish, avoid, mind, suggest, keep, practise. Some are followed by to + verb: want, need, decide, hope, plan, learn, promise.
arabic: بعض الأفعال تتبعها ing: enjoy, finish, avoid, mind, suggest. وبعضها يتبعه to + فعل: want, need, decide, hope, plan, learn.

english: After a preposition we always use -ing: interested in learning, good at cooking, before leaving.
arabic: بعد حرف الجر نستخدم دائمًا ing: interested in learning, good at cooking.

english: ✗ I am interested to learn.   ✓ I am interested in learning.
and (addition), but (contrast), or (choice), so (result), because (reason). because + clause; because of + noun.
arabic: and للإضافة، but للتعارض، or للاختيار، so للنتيجة، because للسبب. because + جملة، وbecause of + اسم.

english: I was tired, so I went to bed.
I stayed home because it was raining.
arabic: بقيتُ في البيت لأنها كانت تمطر.

english: We stayed home because of the rain.
although / even though + clause = but (contrast). however = starts a new sentence with a comma. First, then, after that, finally for steps.
arabic: although + جملة بمعنى «مع أنّ». أمّا however فتبدأ جملة جديدة ويليها فاصلة. وfirst, then, finally لترتيب الخطوات.

english: Although it was cold, we went out.
arabic: مع أن الجو كان باردًا خرجنا.

english: The hotel was expensive. However, it was great.
arabic: كان الفندق غاليًا. ومع ذلك كان رائعًا.

english: First, mix the eggs. Then, add milk. Finally, cook.
arabic: أولًا اخلط البيض. ثم أضف الحليب. وأخيرًا اطبخ.

english: ✗ Although it was cold, but we went out.   ✓ Although it was cold, we went out.
It was raining, ____ I took an umbrella. (so / but)
Although I was tired, I finished the work.
arabic: مع أني كنتُ متعبًا أنهيتُ العمل.

english: Use only one: Although it was cold, we went out.
I was tired, ___ I went to bed early.
I went to bed early ___ I was tired.
He is rich, ___ he is not happy.
We stayed at home ___ the rain.
I am from Jordan, but I live in Dubai.
arabic: أنا من الأردن لكنني أسكن في دبي.

english: I am a student at a university.
I have one brother and two sisters.
In my free time, I like reading and swimming.
arabic: في وقت فراغي أحب القراءة والسباحة.

english: Omar gets up at six o'clock.
He washes his face and brushes his teeth.
He has breakfast with his family at seven.
arabic: يتناول الفطور مع عائلته في السابعة.

english: Omar works in a shop from eight to four.
arabic: يعمل عمر في محلّ من الثامنة إلى الرابعة.

english: In the evening, he plays football with his friends.
arabic: في المساء يلعب كرة القدم مع أصدقائه.

english: He goes to bed at ten o'clock.
How does Omar go to work?
Omar plays football in the morning.
arabic: عمر يلعب كرة القدم في الصباح.

english: Omar goes to bed at ____ o'clock.
It is Saturday. Huda is at the market.
arabic: إنه يوم السبت. هدى في السوق.

english: She wants some fruit and vegetables.
"How much are the apples?" she asks.
"They are two dollars a kilo," says the man.
She buys three kilos of apples and a big watermelon.
arabic: تشتري ثلاثة كيلوغرامات من التفاح وبطيخة كبيرة.

english: Then she buys tomatoes, potatoes and onions.
She pays ten dollars. "Thank you!" says Huda.
arabic: تدفع عشرة دولارات. «شكرًا لك!» تقول هدى.

english: How many kilos of apples does she buy?
Huda is at the market on Friday.
I live in a small house with my family.
arabic: أسكن في بيت صغير مع عائلتي.

english: There are three bedrooms, a kitchen and a living room.
arabic: يوجد ثلاث غرف نوم ومطبخ وغرفة معيشة.

english: My room is next to the kitchen.
There is a bed, a desk and a lamp in my room.
There is a window above my desk.
We have a small garden with flowers and a tree.
arabic: عندنا حديقة صغيرة فيها زهور وشجرة.

english: My cat sleeps under the tree.
The cat sleeps in the kitchen.
There is a ____ above my desk.
Last Friday, my friends and I went to the beach.
arabic: يوم الجمعة الماضي ذهبتُ مع أصدقائي إلى الشاطئ.

english: We left home at eight o'clock in the morning.
The journey took two hours by car.
When we arrived, the weather was sunny and warm.
arabic: عندما وصلنا كان الطقس مشمسًا ودافئًا.

english: We swam in the sea and played volleyball on the sand.
arabic: سبحنا في البحر ولعبنا الكرة الطائرة على الرمل.

english: At lunchtime we ate sandwiches and drank cold juice.
arabic: وقت الغداء أكلنا شطائر وشربنا عصيرًا باردًا.

english: In the afternoon, my friend Khaled took a lot of photos.
arabic: بعد الظهر التقط صديقي خالد صورًا كثيرة.

english: We came home at seven o'clock. We were tired, but very happy.
arabic: عدنا إلى البيت في السابعة. كنا متعبين لكن سعداء جدًا.

english: What did they do at lunchtime?
My best friend is called Mona. We met at school ten years ago.
arabic: أعزّ صديقاتي اسمها منى. تعرّفنا في المدرسة قبل عشر سنوات.

english: She is taller than me and she has long, dark hair.
arabic: هي أطول مني ولها شعر طويل داكن.

english: Mona is very kind and funny. She always makes me laugh.
arabic: منى لطيفة جدًا ومرحة. هي دائمًا تُضحكني.

english: She is the best cook in our group of friends.
arabic: هي أفضل طاهية في مجموعة أصدقائنا.

english: We usually meet at weekends. Sometimes we go shopping, and sometimes we watch a film.
arabic: نلتقي عادةً في عطلة الأسبوع. أحيانًا نذهب للتسوّق وأحيانًا نشاهد فيلمًا.

english: She lives in another city now, so we talk on the phone every evening.
arabic: هي تسكن الآن في مدينة أخرى، لذا نتحدّث بالهاتف كل مساء.

english: Next month, I am going to visit her.
How long have they known each other?
Mona lives in the same city now.
arabic: منى تسكن في المدينة نفسها الآن.

english: They talk on the phone every ____.
This weekend is going to be very busy.
arabic: ستكون عطلة نهاية الأسبوع هذه مزدحمة جدًا.

english: On Friday morning, I'm going to clean the house.
In the afternoon, my cousins are coming for lunch.
arabic: بعد الظهر سيأتي أبناء عمومتي إلى الغداء.

english: My mother is cooking rice and chicken now, and I am helping her.
arabic: أمي تطبخ الأرز والدجاج الآن وأنا أساعدها.

english: On Saturday, we are going to visit our grandparents.
They live in a village near the mountains.
If the weather is nice, we will have a picnic.
arabic: إذا كان الطقس جميلًا فسنقيم نزهة (بيكنيك).

english: I think it will be a lovely weekend!
What is the writer going to do on Friday morning?
The family will have a picnic if the weather is bad.
arabic: ستقيم العائلة نزهة إذا كان الطقس سيئًا.

english: On Saturday they are going to visit their ____.
Last month I travelled from Cairo to Alexandria by train.
arabic: الشهر الماضي سافرتُ من القاهرة إلى الإسكندرية بالقطار.

english: First, I bought a ticket at the station. It was cheaper than a plane ticket.
arabic: أولًا اشتريتُ تذكرة من المحطة. كانت أرخص من تذكرة الطائرة.

english: The train left at nine o'clock and it was on time.
arabic: غادر القطار في التاسعة وكان في موعده.

english: I sat next to a friendly woman. She was going to visit her daughter.
arabic: جلستُ بجانب سيدة ودودة. كانت ذاهبة لزيارة ابنتها.

english: We talked about food, family and travel.
The journey took about two and a half hours.
I looked out of the window and saw fields, small towns and the sea.
arabic: نظرتُ من النافذة ورأيتُ حقولًا وبلدات صغيرة والبحر.

english: I think trains are the best way to travel in Egypt.
arabic: أظن أن القطارات أفضل طريقة للسفر في مصر.

english: Why did the writer choose the train?
The woman was going to visit her ____.
Over the last few years, more and more people have started working from home.
arabic: خلال السنوات القليلة الماضية بدأ عدد متزايد من الناس يعملون من بيوتهم.

english: There are many advantages. You save time and money because you don't have to travel to the office every day.
arabic: له مزايا كثيرة. توفّر الوقت والمال لأنك لست مضطرًا إلى الذهاب إلى المكتب كل يوم.

english: You can also organise your day more flexibly, and spend more time with your family.
arabic: ويمكنك أيضًا تنظيم يومك بمرونة أكبر وقضاء وقت أطول مع عائلتك.

english: However, working from home isn't always easy.
arabic: لكنّ العمل من البيت ليس سهلًا دائمًا.

english: Some people feel lonely because they don't see their colleagues, and it can be difficult to separate work from personal life.
arabic: يشعر بعض الناس بالوحدة لأنهم لا يرون زملاءهم، ومن الصعب الفصل بين العمل والحياة الشخصية.

english: Experts suggest that you should have a quiet place to work, take regular breaks and finish work at a fixed time.
arabic: يقترح الخبراء أن يكون لديك مكان هادئ للعمل، وأن تأخذ استراحات منتظمة، وتنهي العمل في وقت محدّد.

english: Many companies now offer a mix: two or three days at home and the rest in the office.
arabic: كثير من الشركات تقدّم الآن صيغة مختلطة: يومان أو ثلاثة في البيت والباقي في المكتب.

english: Although this system works well for many people, it doesn't suit every job.
arabic: ومع أن هذا النظام ناجح لكثيرين، فإنه لا يناسب كل وظيفة.

english: What is one advantage of working from home?
arabic: ما إحدى مزايا العمل من البيت؟

english: What problem do some people have?
Experts say you should never take breaks.
arabic: يقول الخبراء إنك يجب ألّا تأخذ استراحات أبدًا.

english: Many companies offer a ____ of home and office work.
arabic: تقدّم شركات كثيرة … بين البيت والمكتب.

english: English is the most common language in international business.
arabic: الإنجليزية هي اللغة الأكثر شيوعًا في الأعمال الدولية.

english: If you speak English well, you will have more job opportunities and you might earn a higher salary.
arabic: إذا تكلّمت الإنجليزية جيدًا فستحصل على فرص عمل أكثر وربما على راتب أعلى.

english: Many adults say that speaking is the hardest part. They understand emails but feel nervous in meetings or on the phone.
arabic: يقول كثير من البالغين إن التحدّث هو الجزء الأصعب. يفهمون الرسائل لكنهم يشعرون بالتوتر في الاجتماعات أو على الهاتف.

english: The best way to improve is to practise a little every day.
arabic: أفضل طريقة للتحسّن هي التدرّب قليلًا كل يوم.

english: You could listen to a podcast on your way to work, write short emails in English, or practise common phrases with a colleague.
arabic: يمكنك الاستماع إلى بودكاست في طريقك إلى العمل، وكتابة رسائل قصيرة بالإنجليزية، والتدرّب على العبارات الشائعة مع زميل.

english: Don't be afraid of making mistakes. Mistakes help you learn.
arabic: لا تخف من ارتكاب الأخطاء. الأخطاء تساعدك على التعلّم.

english: After a few months, you will notice that you speak more confidently.
arabic: بعد بضعة أشهر ستلاحظ أنك تتكلّم بثقة أكبر.

english: What do many adults find hardest?
arabic: ما الذي يجده كثير من البالغين أصعب؟

english: What is the best way to improve?
The writer says mistakes are bad for learning.
arabic: يقول الكاتب إن الأخطاء سيئة للتعلّم.

english: After a few months, you will speak more ____.
Last summer, I travelled to Istanbul for a conference. I arrived at the airport three hours before my flight.
arabic: الصيف الماضي سافرتُ إلى إسطنبول لحضور مؤتمر. وصلتُ إلى المطار قبل رحلتي بثلاث ساعات.

english: First, I checked in and left my suitcase at the desk. The woman asked me for my passport and gave me a boarding pass.
arabic: أولًا أنهيتُ إجراءات التسجيل وسلّمتُ حقيبتي. طلبت مني الموظّفة جواز سفري وأعطتني بطاقة الصعود.

english: Then I went through security. I had to take off my belt and put my laptop in a tray.
arabic: ثم مررتُ بالتفتيش الأمني. كان عليّ خلع الحزام ووضع حاسوبي في صينية.

english: While I was waiting at the gate, an announcement said that my flight was delayed by an hour.
arabic: بينما كنتُ أنتظر عند البوابة أعلن الصوت أن رحلتي تأخّرت ساعة.

english: I was a bit annoyed, but I used the time to answer some emails and have a coffee.
arabic: انزعجتُ قليلًا لكنني استغللتُ الوقت في الرد على بعض الرسائل وشرب قهوة.

english: Finally, we boarded the plane and took off. The flight was smooth, and I even slept for a while.
arabic: أخيرًا صعدنا إلى الطائرة وأقلعنا. كانت الرحلة هادئة حتى إنني نمتُ قليلًا.

english: Why did the writer travel to Istanbul?
The writer was very angry about the delay.
arabic: كان الكاتب غاضبًا جدًا من التأخير.

english: He put his laptop in a ____ at security.
Plastic is useful. It is cheap, light and strong, so we use it to make bottles, bags and toys.
arabic: البلاستيك مفيد. فهو رخيص وخفيف وقوي، لذلك نصنع منه الزجاجات والأكياس واللعب.

english: The problem is that plastic does not disappear. A plastic bottle can stay in nature for hundreds of years.
arabic: المشكلة أن البلاستيك لا يختفي. فقد تبقى زجاجة بلاستيكية في الطبيعة مئات السنين.

english: Every year, millions of tonnes of plastic waste end up in the sea.
arabic: كل عام تنتهي ملايين الأطنان من نفايات البلاستيك في البحر.

english: Many animals, such as turtles and fish, mistake plastic for food, and this can make them very sick.
arabic: كثير من الحيوانات، كالسلاحف والأسماك، تظنّ البلاستيك طعامًا، وقد يمرضها ذلك كثيرًا.

english: What can we do? First, we can use fewer plastic bags and take our own bags to the shop.
arabic: ماذا يمكننا أن نفعل؟ أولًا، يمكننا أن نستخدم أكياسًا بلاستيكية أقل ونحمل أكياسنا الخاصة إلى المتجر.

english: Second, we can recycle bottles instead of throwing them away.
arabic: ثانيًا، يمكننا إعادة تدوير الزجاجات بدل رميها.

english: Finally, governments should make laws to reduce plastic waste. If everyone helps, our seas will be cleaner in the future.
arabic: أخيرًا، على الحكومات سنّ قوانين لتقليل نفايات البلاستيك. وإذا ساعد الجميع فستكون بحارنا أنظف في المستقبل.

english: What happens to some sea animals?
The writer says governments should make laws about plastic.
arabic: يقول الكاتب إن على الحكومات سنّ قوانين بشأن البلاستيك.

english: We can ____ bottles instead of throwing them away.
I have a cat. Her name is Luna.
She sleeps on my bed at night.
In the morning, she plays with a ball.
I love my cat very much.
Luna sleeps on the ____ at night.
Last week, my old phone stopped working.
arabic: الأسبوع الماضي توقّف هاتفي القديم عن العمل.

english: The screen was broken and the battery was very weak.
arabic: كانت الشاشة مكسورة والبطارية ضعيفة جدًا.

english: So I went to a shop and looked at many phones.
arabic: فذهبت إلى محلّ ونظرت إلى هواتف كثيرة.

english: Some phones were very expensive, but I did not have much money.
arabic: بعض الهواتف كانت غالية جدًا لكن لم يكن معي مال كثير.

english: The shop assistant showed me a cheaper phone with a good camera.
arabic: أراني البائع هاتفًا أرخص بكاميرا جيدة.

english: I paid by card and took it home.
Now I use it every day to call my family and to study English.
arabic: أستخدمه الآن كل يوم للاتصال بعائلتي ولدراسة الإنجليزية.

english: I am very happy with my choice.
What was wrong with the old phone?
Why did he choose the cheaper phone?
What does he use the phone for?
Many adults need between seven and nine hours of sleep every night.
arabic: يحتاج كثير من البالغين بين سبع وتسع ساعات من النوم كل ليلة.

english: However, a lot of people sleep much less because of work, study or their phones.
arabic: لكن كثيرين ينامون أقل بكثير بسبب العمل أو الدراسة أو هواتفهم.

english: Doctors say that bad sleep can make it harder to concentrate and to remember things.
arabic: يقول الأطباء إن قلّة النوم قد تجعل التركيز والتذكّر أصعب.

english: It can also increase stress and affect your health over time.
arabic: ويمكن أن تزيد التوتّر وتؤثّر في صحتك مع الوقت.

english: To sleep better, try to go to bed at the same time every day.
arabic: لتنام أفضل حاول أن تنام في الوقت نفسه كل يوم.

english: Avoid coffee in the evening, and turn off your phone an hour before bed.
arabic: تجنّب القهوة مساءً وأطفئ هاتفك قبل النوم بساعة.

english: A quiet, dark and cool room also helps.
arabic: وتساعد أيضًا غرفة هادئة ومظلمة وباردة.

english: If you still feel tired after a few weeks, it is a good idea to talk to a doctor.
arabic: وإن بقيتَ متعبًا بعد بضعة أسابيع فمن الجيد أن تستشير طبيبًا.

english: How much sleep do many adults need?
arabic: كم ساعة نوم يحتاج كثير من البالغين؟

english: Which is advice from the text?
Bad sleep can make it harder to remember things.
arabic: قلّة النوم قد تجعل التذكّر أصعب.

english: When should you talk to a doctor?
Last Tuesday, Huda had an interview for a job at a large company.
arabic: يوم الثلاثاء الماضي كان عند هدى مقابلة عمل في شركة كبيرة.

english: She was nervous, so she prepared carefully the night before.
arabic: كانت متوتّرة فحضّرت بعناية في الليلة السابقة.

english: She read about the company and practised answers to common questions.
arabic: قرأت عن الشركة وتدرّبت على الإجابة عن أسئلة شائعة.

english: She arrived ten minutes early and smiled at everyone she met.
arabic: وصلت قبل الموعد بعشر دقائق وابتسمت لكل من قابلته.

english: The manager asked her why she wanted the job.
Huda explained that she enjoys working with people and wants to learn new skills.
arabic: شرحت هدى أنها تحب العمل مع الناس وتريد تعلّم مهارات جديدة.

english: At the end, she asked about training opportunities, which impressed the manager.
arabic: وفي النهاية سألت عن فرص التدريب، وهذا أعجب المدير.

english: Two days later, the company called her and offered her the job.
arabic: وبعد يومين اتّصلت بها الشركة وعرضت عليها الوظيفة.

english: The company called her two ____ later.
Hi! I'm Sara. What's your name?
Hello, Sara. My name is Tom. Nice to meet you.
arabic: مرحبًا يا سارة. اسمي توم. تشرّفتُ بمعرفتك.

english: Nice to meet you too. Where are you from?
I'm from Egypt, but I live in Dubai.
arabic: أنا من مصر لكنني أسكن في دبي.

english: Oh, really? What do you do?
I'm a student. I study English here. What about you?
arabic: أنا طالبة. أدرس الإنجليزية هنا. وأنت؟

english: I'm a teacher. I teach maths at a school.
arabic: أنا معلّم. أدرّس الرياضيات في مدرسة.

english: Good morning. What would you like?
Good morning. I'd like a coffee, please.
arabic: صباح الخير. أريد قهوة من فضلك.

english: Excuse me, what time is it?
Thanks. When does the bus come?
Oh, good. We have thirty minutes.
Let's have a drink at the café.
They will go to a café.
I have a headache and a sore throat.
How long have you had them?
Your temperature is thirty-eight. You should rest and drink a lot of water.
arabic: حرارتك ثمانٍ وثلاثون. ينبغي أن ترتاح وتشرب ماءً كثيرًا.

english: Take these tablets twice a day, after meals.
arabic: خذ هذه الأقراص مرتين في اليوم بعد الوجبات.

english: Since when has he had the problem?
How often should he take the tablets?
The doctor says he should drink a lot of ____.
arabic: تقول الطبيبة إنه ينبغي أن يشرب كثيرًا من …

english: Good evening, Palm Hotel. How can I help you?
arabic: مساء الخير، فندق بالم. كيف أساعدك؟

english: Hello. I'd like to book a room for two nights, please.
arabic: مرحبًا. أريد حجز غرفة لليلتين من فضلك.

english: It's seventy dollars a night, and breakfast is included.
arabic: السعر سبعون دولارًا لليلة، والفطور مشمول.

english: That sounds good. Can I pay by card?
arabic: هذا جيد. هل يمكنني الدفع بالبطاقة؟

english: Yes, of course. May I have your name?
How many nights does he want?
How much is the room per night?
He is arriving on the ____ of March.
Hi, Lina. What are you doing on Saturday?
arabic: مرحبًا يا لينا. ماذا ستفعلين يوم السبت؟

english: There's a new film at the cinema. Do you want to come?
arabic: يوجد فيلم جديد في السينما. هل تريدين المجيء؟

english: Sounds fun! What time does it start?
At half past seven. Shall we meet at six for dinner first?
arabic: في السابعة والنصف. هل نلتقي في السادسة للعشاء أولًا؟

english: Good idea. Let's meet outside the cinema.
They will eat dinner before the film.
Thank you for coming. Could you tell me a little about yourself?
arabic: شكرًا لحضورك. هل يمكنك أن تحدّثني قليلًا عن نفسك؟

english: Of course. I graduated in business last year, and since then I've been working as an assistant in a small company.
arabic: بالطبع. تخرّجتُ في إدارة الأعمال العام الماضي ومنذ ذلك الحين أعمل مساعدًا في شركة صغيرة.

english: I'm organised and I work well in a team. I also speak three languages.
arabic: أنا منظّم وأعمل جيدًا ضمن فريق. وأتكلّم أيضًا ثلاث لغات.

english: Why do you want this job?
Because I'd like to develop my skills in an international company.
arabic: لأنني أريد تطوير مهاراتي في شركة دولية.

english: Where do you see yourself in five years?
arabic: أين ترى نفسك بعد خمس سنوات؟

english: I hope to be a team leader.
Thank you. We'll contact you next week.
arabic: شكرًا لك. سنتواصل معك الأسبوع القادم.

english: How many languages does he speak?
He wants to work in a small local company.
arabic: يريد العمل في شركة محلية صغيرة.

english: In five years he hopes to be a team ____.
arabic: يأمل أن يكون خلال خمس سنوات … فريق.

english: Excuse me, I bought this jacket yesterday, but it doesn't fit.
arabic: عفوًا، اشتريتُ هذه السترة أمس لكنها لا تناسبني.

english: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you have the receipt?
Would you like to exchange it for a bigger size or get a refund?
arabic: هل تريدين استبدالها بمقاس أكبر أم استرداد المبلغ؟

english: No problem. It'll take about five days to appear in your account.
arabic: لا مشكلة. سيستغرق ظهوره في حسابك نحو خمسة أيام.

english: That's fine. Thank you for your help.
The refund will take about ____ days.
Did you have a good holiday?
Yes, it was fantastic. We went to Turkey for ten days.
arabic: نعم، كانت رائعة. ذهبنا إلى تركيا لمدة عشرة أيام.

english: Lucky you! What was the weather like?
It was hot and sunny every day, so we spent most of the time on the beach.
arabic: كان حارًّا ومشمسًا كل يوم، لذا قضينا معظم الوقت على الشاطئ.

english: Did you try the local food?
Of course! The kebabs were delicious. If I could, I would go back next summer.
arabic: بالطبع! كان الكباب لذيذًا. لو استطعتُ لعدتُ الصيف القادم.

english: I'd love to go there one day.
arabic: أتمنى أن أذهب إلى هناك يومًا ما.

english: Karim did not like the food.
Yes, please. I want a blue shirt.
arabic: نعم من فضلك. أريد قميصًا أزرق.

english: Here you are. This one is twenty dollars.
Of course. The changing room is over there.
It fits well. I will take it.
The customer does not buy the shirt.
Excuse me. Is there a pharmacy near here?
arabic: عفوًا. هل توجد صيدلية قريبة من هنا؟

english: Yes. Go straight on and turn left at the traffic lights.
arabic: نعم. امشِ للأمام ثم انعطف يسارًا عند إشارة المرور.

english: No, it is about five minutes on foot.
arabic: لا، تبعد حوالي خمس دقائق مشيًا.

english: Which side of the street is it on?
arabic: على أي جانب من الشارع هي؟

english: It is on the right, next to the bank.
You're welcome. Have a nice day!
What is next to the pharmacy?
The pharmacy is on the left side.
Hello. I ordered a laptop two weeks ago, but it has not arrived.
arabic: مرحبًا. طلبتُ حاسوبًا محمولًا قبل أسبوعين ولم يصل.

english: I'm sorry about that. Could I have your order number, please?
arabic: أعتذر عن ذلك. هل لي برقم الطلب من فضلك؟

english: Thank you. I can see the problem. The package was sent to the wrong address.
arabic: شكرًا. أرى المشكلة. أُرسلت الطرد إلى عنوان خاطئ.

english: That is very disappointing. What can you do?
arabic: هذا مخيّب جدًا. ماذا تستطيعون أن تفعلوا؟

english: We can send a new laptop today, and you will get it within two days.
arabic: نستطيع إرسال حاسوب جديد اليوم وسيصلك خلال يومين.

english: No, delivery is free, and we will give you a ten per cent discount on your next order.
arabic: لا، التوصيل مجاني وسنمنحك خصمًا عشرة بالمئة على طلبك القادم.

english: That sounds fair. Thank you for your help.
When will the new laptop arrive?
The customer must pay for delivery.
arabic: على الزبون أن يدفع ثمن التوصيل.

english: What extra offer does the agent make?
Write 4–6 sentences about yourself: your name, age, country, job or study, and one hobby.
arabic: اكتب ٤–٦ جمل عن نفسك: اسمك وعمرك وبلدك وعملك أو دراستك وهوايتك.

english: My name is Waleid. I am 27 years old. I am from Syria. I study petroleum engineering at a university in India. I like football and reading. I want to speak English well.
arabic: اسمي وليد. عمري ٢٧ سنة. أنا من سوريا. أدرس هندسة البترول في جامعة في الهند. أحب كرة القدم والقراءة. أريد أن أتكلّم الإنجليزية جيدًا.

english: Say where you are from / live
arabic: اذكر من أين أنت / أين تسكن

english: Describe your family: who is in it, and what each person does.
arabic: صِف عائلتك: من فيها وماذا يعمل كل شخص.

english: There are … people in my family.
There are five people in my family. My father is a teacher and my mother is a nurse. I have one brother and one sister. My brother is 20 years old. We live in a small house in the city.
arabic: في عائلتي خمسة أشخاص. أبي معلّم وأمي ممرضة. عندي أخ واحد وأخت واحدة. عمر أخي ٢٠ سنة. نسكن في بيت صغير في المدينة.

english: Name at least one family member
Write about your day: what you do in the morning, afternoon and evening. Use times.
arabic: اكتب عن يومك: ماذا تفعل صباحًا وبعد الظهر ومساءً. استخدم الأوقات.

english: I get up at 6:30. I have breakfast at 7 and then I go to work by bus. I start work at 8:30. In the afternoon, I have lunch with my colleagues. I finish work at 5. In the evening, I study English for one hour. I go to bed at 11.
arabic: أستيقظ في 6:30. أتناول الفطور في 7 ثم أذهب إلى العمل بالحافلة. أبدأ العمل في 8:30. بعد الظهر أتناول الغداء مع زملائي. أنهي العمل في 5. في المساء أدرس الإنجليزية ساعة. أنام في 11.

english: Write a short message to a friend. Invite them to do something this weekend. Say where, when, and ask them to reply.
arabic: اكتب رسالة قصيرة لصديق تدعوه فيها لفعل شيء هذا الأسبوع. اذكر المكان والوقت واطلب منه الرد.

english: Would you like to … on Saturday?
Let me know if you can come.

Hi Sara,
Would you like to go to the beach on Saturday? We can meet at the bus station at 9 a.m. We can swim and have lunch there. Let me know if you can come.
See you soon!
Omar
arabic: مرحبًا سارة، هل تودّين الذهاب إلى الشاطئ يوم السبت؟ يمكننا أن نلتقي في محطة الحافلات في ٩ صباحًا. نسبح ونتناول الغداء هناك. أخبريني إن كنتِ تستطيعين الحضور. أراك قريبًا! عمر

english: Make an invitation (Would you like…? / Let's…)

arabic: اذكر الزمان والمكان بـ on / at

english: Write about a holiday or trip you had. Use the past simple: where you went, what you did, and what you liked.
arabic: اكتب عن عطلة أو رحلة قمت بها. استخدم الماضي البسيط: أين ذهبت، ماذا فعلت، وما الذي أعجبك.

english: I stayed in a hotel for … days.

Last summer I went to Istanbul with my family. We stayed in a small hotel for five days. We visited the old mosques and ate delicious food. The weather was hot and sunny. I really liked the market because the people were friendly.
arabic: الصيف الماضي ذهبت إلى إسطنبول مع عائلتي. أقمنا في فندق صغير خمسة أيام. زرنا المساجد القديمة وأكلنا طعامًا لذيذًا. كان الطقس حارًّا ومشمسًا. أعجبني السوق كثيرًا لأن الناس كانوا ودودين.

english: Use past simple verbs (went, visited, was…)
Say when (last year / two years ago)
Describe the city or town where you live. What is there? What do you like and not like?
arabic: صِف المدينة التي تسكن فيها. ماذا يوجد فيها؟ ما الذي يعجبك وما الذي لا يعجبك؟

english: There is a … and there are …
It is a big / small city.

I live in Dhanbad. It is a small city in India. There is a big university and there are many shops near the station. I like it because the people are kind and the food is cheap. However, the weather is very hot in summer and there is a lot of traffic.
arabic: أسكن في دانباد. إنها مدينة صغيرة في الهند. توجد جامعة كبيرة وتوجد محلات كثيرة قرب المحطة. تعجبني لأن الناس طيبون والطعام رخيص. لكن الطقس حارّ جدًّا في الصيف وفيه ازدحام كثير.

english: Say what you like / don't like
arabic: قل ما تحب وما لا تحب

english: Join ideas with but / because / however
Do you think working from home is better than working in an office? Write a short paragraph with your opinion, two reasons and a conclusion.
arabic: هل ترى أن العمل من المنزل أفضل من العمل في المكتب؟ اكتب فقرة قصيرة برأيك وسببين وخاتمة.

english: In my opinion, working from home is better for most people. Firstly, you save time and money because you do not travel to the office. Secondly, you can organise your day in a more flexible way. For example, I can study English in the morning and finish my work in the afternoon. On the other hand, some people feel lonely at home. To sum up, I think a mix of home and office days is the best choice.
arabic: في رأيي العمل من المنزل أفضل لمعظم الناس. أولًا توفّر الوقت والمال لأنك لا تسافر إلى المكتب. ثانيًا تنظّم يومك بمرونة أكبر؛ فمثلًا أستطيع دراسة الإنجليزية صباحًا وإنهاء عملي بعد الظهر. من ناحية أخرى يشعر بعض الناس بالوحدة في البيت. خلاصة القول: أرى أن الجمع بين أيام المنزل وأيام المكتب هو الأفضل.

english: State your opinion (In my opinion… / I think…)
Write a formal email to a company. You saw a course advertised and want information about the price, dates and how to register.
arabic: اكتب رسالة رسمية إلى شركة. رأيت إعلانًا لدورة وتريد معلومات عن السعر والمواعيد وطريقة التسجيل.

english: I am writing to enquire about …
I look forward to hearing from you.

Dear Sir or Madam,
I am writing to enquire about the English course advertised on your website. Could you please tell me the price and the start date? I would also like to know how I can register. I look forward to hearing from you.
Kind regards,
Waleid Ahmad
arabic: سيدي / سيدتي، أكتب للاستفسار عن دورة اللغة الإنجليزية المعلن عنها على موقعكم. هل تتفضّلون بإخباري بالسعر وتاريخ البدء؟ كما أودّ معرفة كيفية التسجيل. أتطلّع إلى سماع ردّكم. مع خالص التحية، وليد أحمد

english: End with Kind regards + your name
Write an email to your manager. Your report will be late. Say sorry, explain why, and give a new date.
arabic: اكتب رسالة لمديرك. تقريرك سيتأخر. اعتذر واشرح السبب وأعطِ موعدًا جديدًا.

english: I am sorry to tell you that …

Dear Mr. Haddad,
I am sorry to tell you that the sales report will be late. This is because I am still waiting for the final numbers from the finance team. I will send it to you by Friday at noon. Thank you for your understanding.
Best regards,
Rana
arabic: عزيزي السيد حداد، يؤسفني أن أخبرك أن تقرير المبيعات سيتأخّر. وذلك لأنني ما زلت أنتظر الأرقام النهائية من فريق المالية. سأرسله إليك بحلول الجمعة ظهرًا. شكرًا لتفهّمك. مع أطيب التحيات، رنا
agree فعل، فلا نضيف am (بالعربية «أنا موافق» اسم).

id: She go to work every day.
arabic: مع he / she / it نضيف s أو es للفعل في المضارع البسيط.

english: I am / you, we, they are / he, she, it is.
arabic: نستخدم are مع you/we/they، و is مع he/she/it.

id: I am work in a bank.
english: Do not add "am" before a normal verb.
arabic: لا نضع am قبل الفعل العادي في المضارع البسيط.

english: "Discuss" is followed directly by the object.
arabic: الفعل discuss يأتي بعده المفعول مباشرة بدون about.

english: Information, advice, furniture, equipment are uncountable: no -s.
arabic: information / advice / furniture / equipment غير معدودة، فلا نضيف s.

id: He is married with a teacher.

arabic: العمر مع to be: I am 25 years old.

english: Use "for" with a length of time; "since" with a starting point.
arabic: نستخدم for مع المدة، وsince مع نقطة البداية.

id: I have a meeting in Monday.

english: After do / does / did use the base verb.
arabic: بعد do / does / did نستخدم الفعل بصيغته الأصلية.

english: After didn't use the base verb.
a before consonant sounds; an before vowel sounds.
arabic: نستخدم an قبل الأصوات الصائتة، وa قبل الأصوات الساكنة.

id: The food is very much good.

english: People, police, children take plural verbs.
arabic: كلمة people وchildren تأخذ فعلًا جمعًا (are).

english: Start every sentence with a capital letter and end it with . ? or !
arabic: ابدأ كل جملة بحرف كبير وأنهِها بنقطة أو علامة استفهام أو تعجّب.

english: Always write "I" as a capital letter.
arabic: اكتب ضمير I دائمًا بحرف كبير.

english: Use a comma after Hello / Firstly / However and between items in a list.
arabic: ضع فاصلة بعد Hello وFirstly وHowever وبين عناصر القائمة.

english: English has no "and" at the start of every sentence: connect short ideas with and, but, because, so.
arabic: اربط الجمل القصيرة بـ and / but / because / so بدل جمل قصيرة متقطّعة.

english: Meet new colleagues and clients confidently.
I'm in charge of the sales team.
I work in the finance department.
How long have you been with the company?
Did you have a good weekend?
arabic: هل قضيتَ عطلة نهاية أسبوع جيدة؟

english: Let me introduce you to my colleague, Sam.
arabic: اسمح لي أن أعرّفك بزميلي سام.

english: It was great talking to you.
Hello, I'm James from Delta Trading. Nice to meet you.
arabic: مرحبًا، أنا جيمس من شركة دلتا للتجارة. تشرّفتُ بمعرفتك.

english: Nice to meet you too. I'm Nadia. I work in the marketing department.
arabic: وأنا أيضًا. أنا نادية. أعمل في قسم التسويق.

english: For three years. And what do you do at Delta?
arabic: منذ ثلاث سنوات. وماذا تعمل في دلتا؟

english: I'm in charge of the sales team. How was your trip here?
arabic: أنا مسؤول عن فريق المبيعات. كيف كانت رحلتك إلى هنا؟

english: It was fine, thanks. The flight was a bit late, but it was comfortable.
arabic: كانت جيدة شكرًا. تأخّرت الرحلة قليلًا لكنها كانت مريحة.

english: Let me introduce you to my colleague, Sam. He's our technical manager.
arabic: اسمح لي أن أعرّفك بزميلي سام. هو مدير القسم التقني.

english: Hello, I'm James. Nice to meet you.
Too short. Add "Nice to meet you" and your name.
arabic: مقتضب جدًا. أضف عبارة الترحيب واسمك.

english: "Me too" does not answer "Nice to meet you" naturally.
arabic: عبارة Me too لا تناسب هذا الموقف.

english: Clear job + a question back keeps the conversation going.
arabic: وظيفتك واضحة وسؤال مقابل يُبقي الحديث.

english: Grammar: I work in a company.
arabic: القاعدة: I work in a company بلا am.

english: Did you have a good weekend?
Correct but it ends the conversation.
Natural way to close and stay connected.
Not natural. Say: I have to go now.
arabic: غير طبيعية. نقول: I have to go now.

english: Make and answer calls clearly and politely.
arabic: اتصل وأجب على المكالمات بوضوح وأدب.

english: Hello, this is Omar from ABC Company.
arabic: مرحبًا، معك عمر من شركة ABC.

english: Could I speak to Ms. Hana, please?
arabic: هل يمكنني التحدّث إلى السيدة هناء من فضلك؟

english: I'm afraid she isn't available at the moment.
Could you hold on a moment, please?
Could you speak more slowly, please?
arabic: هل تتكلّم ببطء أكثر من فضلك؟

english: Good morning, Delta Trading. How can I help you?
arabic: صباح الخير، دلتا للتجارة. كيف أساعدك؟

english: Good morning. This is Omar from ABC Company. Could I speak to Ms. Hana, please?
arabic: صباح الخير. معك عمر من شركة ABC. هل يمكنني التحدّث إلى السيدة هناء؟

english: I'm afraid she isn't available at the moment. Can I take a message?
arabic: للأسف هي غير متاحة الآن. هل آخذ رسالة؟

english: Yes, please. I'm calling about the invoice. Could she call me back this afternoon?
arabic: نعم من فضلك. أتّصل بخصوص الفاتورة. هل يمكنها معاودة الاتصال بي بعد الظهر؟

english: Of course. Could you spell your surname, please?
arabic: بالطبع. هل تتهجّى اسم عائلتك من فضلك؟

english: Thank you, Mr. Haddad. I'll give her the message.
arabic: شكرًا لك يا سيد حداد. سأعطيها الرسالة.
غير مهذّب. استخدم Could I speak to…؟

english: I'm afraid Mr. Hassan is in a meeting. Can I take a message?
arabic: للأسف السيد حسان في اجتماع. هل آخذ رسالة؟

english: You should give your name and number.
Sorry, could you spell your name, please?
arabic: عفوًا، هل تتهجّى اسمك من فضلك؟

english: I am writing to enquire about…
I would like to confirm our meeting on Monday.
Could you please send me the details?
arabic: هل يمكنك إرسال التفاصيل لي من فضلك؟

english: I look forward to hearing from you.
Mark, did you send the email to the client?
arabic: مارك، هل أرسلتَ الرسالة إلى العميل؟

english: Not yet. I'm still writing it. How do I start?
arabic: ليس بعد. ما زلتُ أكتبها. كيف أبدأ؟

english: Start with "Dear Mr. Rashid," and then say: Thank you for your email.
arabic: ابدأ بـ «Dear Mr. Rashid،» ثم قل: Thank you for your email.

english: And then I write what I need?
Yes. For example: Could you please send me the details by Friday?
arabic: نعم. مثلًا: Could you please send me the details by Friday?

english: Write: I look forward to hearing from you. Then: Kind regards, and your name.
arabic: اكتب: I look forward to hearing from you. ثم Kind regards، واسمك.

english: Which opening is best for an email to a client you do not know?
arabic: أي افتتاحية الأنسب لرسالة إلى عميل لا تعرفه؟

english: Formal and correct when you do not know the name.
arabic: رسمية وصحيحة حين لا تعرف الاسم.

english: Too casual for a new client.
You want to ask for information. Which sentence is the most polite?
arabic: تريد طلب معلومات. أي جملة الأكثر أدبًا؟

english: You attach a file. What do you write?
How do you end the email?
I would like to confirm our meeting on Monday at 10 a.m. in your office.
arabic: أودّ تأكيد اجتماعنا يوم الاثنين في العاشرة صباحًا في مكتبكم.

english: Could you please send me the agenda by Friday?
arabic: هل يمكنك إرسال جدول الأعمال لي بحلول الجمعة؟

english: Share opinions, agree and disagree politely.
The purpose of this meeting is to discuss the budget.
arabic: الغرض من هذا الاجتماع مناقشة الميزانية.

english: What do you think about this idea?
I see your point, but I think we need more time.
arabic: أفهم وجهة نظرك لكنني أرى أننا نحتاج مزيدًا من الوقت.

english: Let's move on to the next item.
To sum up, we agreed to start in June.
arabic: خلاصة القول، اتفقنا على البدء في يونيو.

english: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started. The purpose of this meeting is to discuss the new project.
arabic: صباح الخير للجميع. لنبدأ. الغرض من هذا الاجتماع مناقشة المشروع الجديد.

english: Could I add something before we start? I think we should include the marketing team.
arabic: هل يمكنني إضافة شيء قبل أن نبدأ؟ أظن أن علينا إشراك فريق التسويق.

english: That's a good idea. What do you think, Peter, about starting in May?
arabic: فكرة جيدة. ما رأيك يا بيتر بالبدء في مايو؟

english: I see your point, but I think June is better. We need more time to prepare.
arabic: أفهم وجهة نظرك لكنني أرى أن يونيو أفضل. نحتاج مزيدًا من الوقت للتحضير.

english: That's fair. I agree with you. Let's start in June.
arabic: هذا عادل. أتفق معك. لنبدأ في يونيو.

english: Great. Let's move on to the budget.
To sum up, we'll start in June and invite the marketing team. Let's schedule a follow-up meeting next week.
arabic: خلاصة القول: سنبدأ في يونيو وندعو فريق التسويق. ولنحدّد اجتماع متابعة الأسبوع القادم.

english: A colleague suggests starting in May. You prefer June.
arabic: يقترح زميل البدء في مايو وأنت تفضّل يونيو.

english: Someone is talking, and you have an important point.
The discussion is going off topic.
Open, structure and close a short talk.
Good morning, everyone. Thank you for coming.
Today I'm going to talk about our sales results.
As you can see, sales increased by 15%.
This brings me to my next point.
In conclusion, we had a very good year.
arabic: في الختام، كان عامًا جيدًا جدًا.

english: I'll get back to you on that.
Good morning, everyone. Thank you for coming. Today I'm going to talk about our sales results.
arabic: صباح الخير للجميع. شكرًا لحضوركم. سأتحدّث اليوم عن نتائج مبيعاتنا.

english: My presentation has three parts: the results, the problems and the plan.
arabic: يتكوّن عرضي من ثلاثة أجزاء: النتائج والمشكلات والخطة.

english: Let's look at this chart. As you can see, sales increased by fifteen per cent.
arabic: لننظر إلى هذا الرسم. كما ترون زادت المبيعات خمسة عشر بالمئة.

english: This brings me to my next point: the plan for next year.
arabic: وهذا يقودني إلى نقطتي التالية: خطة العام القادم.

english: In conclusion, we had a very good year. Thank you for listening. Are there any questions?
arabic: في الختام كان عامًا جيدًا جدًا. شكرًا لاستماعكم. هل من أسئلة؟

english: Yes. What was the biggest problem?
That's a good question. The biggest problem was delivery times. I'll get back to you with the exact numbers.
arabic: سؤال جيد. أكبر مشكلة كانت مواعيد التسليم. سأعود إليك بالأرقام الدقيقة.

english: You are starting a presentation. What do you say?
Say: I'm going to talk about…
arabic: قل: I'm going to talk about…

english: You want to show a graph.
Someone asks a question and you don't know the answer.
arabic: سأل أحدهم سؤالًا لا تعرف إجابته.

english: Add what you will do next.
Help customers and handle problems politely.
How can I help you today?
Let me check that for you.
Could I have your order number, please?
arabic: هل لي برقم طلبك من فضلك؟

english: Your refund will arrive in five working days.
arabic: سيصلك المبلغ المسترد خلال خمسة أيام عمل.

english: Is there anything else I can help you with?
arabic: هل هناك شيء آخر أساعدك فيه؟

english: I'd like to make a complaint.
Good afternoon. How can I help you today?
Hello. I ordered a phone last week, but it hasn't arrived yet.
arabic: مرحبًا. طلبتُ هاتفًا الأسبوع الماضي ولم يصل بعد.

english: I'm sorry for the inconvenience. Could I have your order number, please?
arabic: أعتذر عن الإزعاج. هل لي برقم طلبك من فضلك؟

english: Thank you. Let me check that for you. One moment, please.
arabic: شكرًا لك. دعيني أتحقّق من ذلك. لحظة من فضلك.

english: Thank you for your patience. The delivery was delayed, but it will arrive tomorrow.
arabic: شكرًا لصبرك. تأخّر التسليم لكنه سيصل غدًا.

english: The customer says: 'My order is late and I am angry!'
arabic: يقول العميل: طلبي متأخر وأنا غاضب!

english: Never say this to a customer.
Can sound rude. Show empathy first.
arabic: قد تبدو فظّة. أظهر التفهّم أولًا.

english: The problem needs time to solve.
Ask people to repeat, slow down and explain.
Sorry, could you repeat that, please?
Do you mean the Friday meeting?
Let me check that I understand.
Could you write it down, please?
Just to confirm, the report is due on Monday?
arabic: للتأكيد فقط، موعد التقرير يوم الاثنين؟

english: Dina, I need the report by the end of the day, and please copy the whole team.
arabic: دينا، أحتاج التقرير بنهاية اليوم، ويرجى إرسال نسخة لكل الفريق.

english: Sorry, could you speak a little more slowly? What does 'copy the team' mean?
arabic: عذرًا، هل تتكلّم أبطأ قليلًا؟ ماذا تعني copy the team؟

english: It means: send the email to everybody in the team, too.
arabic: تعني: أرسلها إلى كل أعضاء الفريق أيضًا.

english: I see. Just to confirm, you need the report today, and I send it to you and to the team?
arabic: فهمت. للتأكيد فقط، تحتاج التقرير اليوم وأرسله إليك وإلى الفريق؟

english: Could you write the deadline in an email, please? I don't want to forget.
arabic: هل يمكنك كتابة الموعد النهائي في رسالة؟ لا أريد أن أنسى.

english: Of course. I'll send it now.
You didn't hear what your colleague said.
You want to be sure you understood.
Better to use a full sentence.
Ask politely, make offers, reach agreement.
arabic: اطلب بأدب وقدّم عروضًا وتوصّل إلى اتفاق.

english: Could you possibly send it today?
Would it be possible to change the date?
I was wondering if you could give us a discount.
arabic: كنتُ أتساءل إن كان بإمكانكم منحنا خصمًا.

english: I'd appreciate it if you could reply soon.
We can offer you a ten per cent discount.
arabic: يمكننا أن نمنحك خصمًا بنسبة عشرة بالمئة.

english: That's a bit more than we expected.
How about a delivery in two weeks?
We'd like to think about it.
I'm afraid we can't agree to that.
arabic: للأسف لا نستطيع الموافقة على ذلك.

english: Thank you for sending the offer. I was wondering if you could give us a discount.
arabic: شكرًا لإرسالك العرض. كنتُ أتساءل إن كان بإمكانكم منحنا خصمًا.

english: We can offer you a five per cent discount for an order of five hundred units.
arabic: يمكننا منحك خصمًا بنسبة خمسة بالمئة لطلب من خمسمئة وحدة.

english: That's a bit less than we expected. Would it be possible to get ten per cent?
arabic: هذا أقل مما توقّعنا قليلًا. هل من الممكن الحصول على عشرة بالمئة؟

english: I'm afraid ten per cent is too high. How about seven per cent and free delivery?
arabic: للأسف عشرة بالمئة كثيرة جدًا. ما رأيك بسبعة بالمئة مع توصيل مجاني؟

english: That sounds fair. Let's meet in the middle. Seven per cent and free delivery.
arabic: يبدو عادلًا. لنتّفق في منتصف الطريق: سبعة بالمئة مع توصيل مجاني.

english: Agreed. I'll send you the contract today.
Thank you. I'd appreciate it if you could send it before noon.
arabic: شكرًا. سأكون ممتنة لو أرسلته قبل الظهر.

english: You want a discount. Which is the best way to ask?
The supplier offers 5% but you wanted 10%.
You lose the chance to negotiate.
Say "We'd like to think about it."
arabic: قل: We'd like to think about it.

english: You need a decision by the end of the day.
Check in, order food and be a good host or guest.
arabic: سجّل دخولك واطلب الطعام وكن مضيفًا أو ضيفًا لبقًا.

english: I'd like to check in, please.
I have a reservation under the name Ahmed.
Could you recommend a good restaurant?
Could we have the bill, please?
arabic: هل يمكننا الحصول على الفاتورة من فضلك؟

english: Good evening. Do you have a reservation?
Yes, I have a reservation under the name Ahmed. A table for four, please.
arabic: نعم، عندي حجز باسم أحمد. طاولة لأربعة من فضلك.

english: This way, please. Here are the menus.
arabic: من هنا من فضلك. هذه قوائم الطعام.

english: Thank you. What would you recommend?
The grilled fish is very popular today.
That sounds good. I'll have the grilled fish, please.
arabic: يبدو جيدًا. سآخذ السمك المشوي من فضلك.

english: Water for everyone, please. And later, could we have the bill?
arabic: ماء للجميع من فضلك. ولاحقًا هل نحصل على الفاتورة؟

english: You invited the clients to dinner.
You invited them, so offer to pay.
Report your work and manage deadlines.
arabic: أخبر عن عملك وأدِر المواعيد النهائية.

english: I'll send it by the end of the day.
Could you give me an update?
I'll follow up with you tomorrow.
Let me know if you need anything.
I need more time. Can we extend the deadline?
arabic: أحتاج وقتًا أكثر. هل يمكن تمديد الموعد؟

english: Sorry, I'll be late. I'll be there in ten minutes.
arabic: آسف، سأتأخّر. سأصل خلال عشر دقائق.

english: Rana, could you give me an update on the sales report?
arabic: رنا، هل يمكنك إعطائي آخر المستجدات عن تقرير المبيعات؟

english: I'm working on it. I've finished the first part, but we're a bit behind schedule.
arabic: أعمل عليه. أنهيتُ الجزء الأول لكننا متأخرون قليلًا عن الجدول.

english: I'm still waiting for the numbers from the finance team.
arabic: ما زلتُ أنتظر الأرقام من فريق المالية.

english: I'll send it by the end of the day tomorrow, if that's all right.
arabic: سأرسله بنهاية يوم الغد إن كان ذلك مناسبًا.

english: That's fine. Let me know if you need anything.
arabic: لا بأس. أخبريني إن احتجتِ شيئًا.

english: Thank you. I'll follow up with you tomorrow.
Your boss asks: Could you give me an update?
arabic: يسألك مديرك: هل تعطيني آخر المستجدات؟

english: A colleague asks about the meeting time.
You will be late for work.
The test was a piece of cake.
He told a joke to break the ice.
I am a bit under the weather today.
We eat out once in a blue moon.
I must hit the books tonight.
cost an arm and a leg

id: idioms/cost an arm and a leg
english: That car costs an arm and a leg.
Let's make sure we are on the same page.
We are tired. Let's call it a day.
the ball is in your court

id: idioms/the ball is in your court
english: I made my offer. The ball is in your court.
Let's get the ball rolling with the first item.
In the long run, saving money is wise.
The plan failed, so we are back to square one.
arabic: فشلت الخطة فعدنا إلى نقطة البداية.

english: I had to bite the bullet and call him.
Who spilled the beans about the party?
Hang in there. It will get better.
Using this app is not rocket science.
The manager does everything by the book.
arabic: المدير يفعل كل شيء حسب القواعد.

english: We need to think outside the box.
In a nutshell, the project was a success.
Please keep an eye on my bag.
He got cold feet before the interview.
She is always on top of things at work.
arabic: هي دائمًا مسيطرة على الأمور في العمل.

english: Study every day. No pain, no gain.
arabic: ادرس كل يوم. لا مكسب بلا تعب.

english: I get up at six every day.
Turn off your phone in the meeting.
I am looking for my keys.
Put on your coat. It's cold.
The plane takes off at nine.
I will pick you up at the station.
I want to find out the truth.
They set up a new company.
Please carry on with your work.
Hand in your homework on Monday.
I work out at the gym twice a week.
He pointed out a mistake in the report.
Look up the word in a dictionary.
We check in at two o'clock.
Get on the bus at the next stop.
I get off at the station.
My car broke down on the way.
He turned down the job offer.
She brought up an important issue.
I can't figure out this problem.
I will sort out the problem today.
I need to catch up on my work.
We need to make a decision today.
I want to make an appointment with the doctor.
She makes good money as a designer.
I do my homework after dinner.
We do the shopping on Saturdays.
We do business with many countries.
Let's take a break for ten minutes.
Can I take a photo here?
We took a taxi to the airport.
We have a meeting at three.
I must catch the 8 o'clock bus.
Please pay attention to the teacher.
Can you give me some advice?
Let's keep in touch by email.
Many Arabic dialects have no /p/, so "park" can sound like "bark". Put your lips together and release a small puff of air for /p/ — hold a tissue in front of your mouth: it should move.
arabic: كثير من اللهجات العربية ليس فيها صوت /p/ فيُنطق park كأنه bark. أطبق الشفتين ثم أطلق نفَسًا خفيفًا مع /p/ — ضع ورقة أمام فمك: يجب أن تتحرك.

english: For /v/ and /f/ the top teeth touch the bottom lip. /v/ uses the voice (feel the buzz in your throat), /f/ is only air.
arabic: مع /v/ و/f/ تلمس الأسنان العليا الشفة السفلى. /v/ مجهور (تحسّ بالاهتزاز في الحلق) و/f/ هواء فقط.

english: Put the tip of your tongue between your teeth. /θ/ (think, three) is air only; /ð/ (this, that) has voice. Do not replace them with /s/, /t/ or /z/, /d/.
arabic: ضع طرف اللسان بين الأسنان. /θ/ (think, three) هواء فقط، و/ð/ (this, that) مجهور. لا تستبدلهما بـ s أو t أو z أو d.

english: English changes meaning with vowel length and quality: ship ≠ sheep, bit ≠ beat. Make the long vowel longer and tighter, the short one quick and relaxed.
arabic: في الإنجليزية يتغيّر المعنى بتغيّر طول الصائت ونوعه: ship ≠ sheep. اجعل الطويل أطول وأشدّ والقصير سريعًا ومسترخيًا.

english: English /r/ is not rolled: curl the tongue back without touching the roof of the mouth. For /l/ the tongue tip touches behind the top teeth.
arabic: حرف /r/ الإنجليزي ليس مكرّرًا (ليس كراء العربية): قوّس اللسان للخلف دون لمس سقف الفم. أما /l/ فيلمس طرف اللسان خلف الأسنان العليا.

english: In "sing" the sound is one nasal sound /ŋ/ — do not add a hard /g/ after it and do not replace it with /n/.
arabic: في كلمة sing صوت أنفي واحد /ŋ/ — لا تضف /g/ قاسية بعده ولا تستبدله بـ /n/.

english: Say your name, age, country, job or study, and one thing you like.
arabic: قل اسمك وعمرك وبلدك وعملك أو دراستك وشيئًا تحبه.

english: Hello! My name is Omar. I am twenty-five years old. I am from Syria and I work in a bank. I like football and I want to improve my English.
arabic: مرحبًا! اسمي عمر. عمري خمس وعشرون سنة. أنا من سوريا وأعمل في مصرف. أحب كرة القدم وأريد تحسين إنجليزيتي.

english: Talk about the people in your family and what they do.
arabic: تحدّث عن أفراد عائلتك وماذا يعملون.

english: There are five people in my family. My father is a teacher and my mother is a nurse. I have one brother and one sister. We live in a small house.
arabic: في عائلتي خمسة أشخاص. أبي معلّم وأمي ممرضة. عندي أخ وأخت. نسكن في بيت صغير.

english: Describe your day from morning to evening. Use times.
arabic: صِف يومك من الصباح إلى المساء. استخدم الأوقات.

english: I get up at six. I have breakfast and then I go to work by bus. I start work at eight and finish at four. In the evening I study English and watch TV. I go to bed at eleven.
arabic: أستيقظ في السادسة. أتناول الفطور ثم أذهب إلى العمل بالحافلة. أبدأ العمل في الثامنة وأنتهي في الرابعة. في المساء أدرس الإنجليزية وأشاهد التلفاز. أنام في الحادية عشرة.

english: Say what food you like and don't like, and what you eat for breakfast.
arabic: قل ما الطعام الذي تحبه وما لا تحبه وماذا تأكل في الفطور.

english: I like … but I don't like …
My favourite food is rice with chicken. I like fruit, but I don't like fish. For breakfast I usually have bread, cheese and tea.
arabic: طعامي المفضّل الأرز مع الدجاج. أحب الفواكه لكن لا أحب السمك. في الفطور آكل عادةً الخبز والجبن والشاي.

english: Say what you did last weekend. Use the past simple.
arabic: قل ماذا فعلتَ في عطلة نهاية الأسبوع الماضية. استخدم الماضي البسيط.

english: Last weekend I visited my grandparents. On Saturday we had lunch together and talked for a long time. On Sunday I went to the park with my cousins. It was a lovely weekend and I really enjoyed it.
arabic: في عطلة الأسبوع الماضية زرتُ جدّيّ. يوم السبت تناولنا الغداء معًا وتحدّثنا طويلًا. يوم الأحد ذهبت إلى الحديقة مع أولاد عمّي. كانت عطلة جميلة واستمتعت بها كثيرًا.

english: Describe the place where you live: what there is, what you like, what you don't.
arabic: صِف المكان الذي تسكن فيه: ما الموجود فيه وما يعجبك وما لا يعجبك.

english: I live in a medium-sized city near the sea. There is a big market and there are many cafés. I like it because the people are friendly. However, there is a lot of traffic in the morning.
arabic: أسكن في مدينة متوسطة قرب البحر. يوجد سوق كبير ومقاهٍ كثيرة. تعجبني لأن الناس ودودون. لكن هناك ازدحامًا كثيرًا في الصباح.

english: Describe a friend: appearance, personality, and why you like them.
arabic: صِف صديقًا: شكله وشخصيته ولماذا تحبه.
